header.title: Gittin: AI translation (Claude)
header.author: Babylonian Talmud
header.source: Translated by Claude (claude-opus-5-5, Anthropic) from the library's urn:rabbinic:gittin:vilna, from the Wikisource Talmud Bavli, in Sefaria's export (CC BY-SA), one English line for each line of the original. Only some passages are translated so far: those that the Atlas of Ancient Myth, Magic in the Ancient Texts and the demons-and-angels study cite.
header.statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.

notes.68a.5: Ashmedai is Asmodeus. 68a.5: 'here' is Babylonia and 'the West' the Land of Israel; the Western word shiddeta is usually taken as carriages or chests. 68a.6: Shihin is a place name. 68a.8: כבשינהו אהדדי, 'press them against each other', may mean 'subdue/torment them one with another'. 68a.12: מיפרזל 'struggling' is uncertain. 68b.5: 'that man' is the idiom for 'you'. 68b.6: the 'wild cock' is commonly identified with the hoopoe, and 68b.7 refers to the Aramaic rendering of that bird's name as naggar tura. 68b.15: בלעיה may be 'swallowed it' (the ring) or 'swallowed him' (Solomon). 68b.16: גונדו is obscure; 'cloak' is a guess (a garment or girdle; some take it as a vessel).

nodes.text: “I made myself male and female singers, and the delights of humankind, *shiddah* and *shiddot*” (Ecclesiastes 2:8). “Male and female singers”: these are kinds of music. “And the delights of humankind”: these are pools and bathhouses. “*Shiddah* and *shiddot*”: here they render it *shida* and *shidatin* [a demon and demonesses]; in the West they say *shiddeta*.
Rabbi Yohanan said: There were three hundred kinds of *shedim* [demons] in Shihin, but the *shida* itself, I do not know what it is.

The Master said: “Here they render it *shida* and *shidatin*.” What did he need a demon and demonesses for? As it is written: “And the house, when it was being built, was built of whole stone from the quarry, etc.” (1 Kings 6:7). He said to the Rabbis: How shall I do [it]? They said to him: There is the *shamir* [a stone-cutting creature] that Moses brought for the stones of the ephod.

He said to them: Where is it to be found? They said to him: Bring a demon and demonesses and press them against each other; perhaps they know and will reveal [it] to you. He brought a demon and demonesses and pressed them against each other. They said: We do not know; perhaps Ashmedai, king of the demons, knows.

He said to them: Where is he? They said to him: He is on such-and-such a mountain. He has dug himself a pit and filled it with water, and covered it with a rock and sealed it with his seal. And every day he goes up to heaven and studies in the academy of heaven, and comes down to earth and studies in the academy of earth, and comes and inspects his seal, and uncovers it and drinks, and covers it and seals it, and goes.

He sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He gave him a chain on which the Name was engraved, and a ring on which the Name was engraved, and tufts of wool, and skins of wine. He went [and] dug a pit below and drained off the water, and stopped [the holes] with the tufts of wool; and he dug a pit above and poured in the wine, and filled [them] in. He went up [and] sat in a tree.

When he came, he inspected the seal, uncovered it, [and] found it wine. He said: It is written: “Wine is a mocker, strong drink is rowdy, and whoever strays by it will not be wise” (Proverbs 20:1); and it is written: “Harlotry and wine and new wine take away the heart” (Hosea 4:11). He did not drink. When he grew thirsty, he could not hold out; he drank, became drunk, and slept.
He came down, came, threw the chain on him, [and] locked it. When he woke, he was struggling. He said to him: The Name of your Master is upon you! The Name of your Master is upon you!
As he was leading him along, he came to a palm tree, rubbed against it, [and] knocked it down. He came to a house [and] knocked it down. He came to the hut of a certain widow. She came out
[and] pleaded with him. He bent his body away from it, [and] a bone in him broke. He said: This is what is written: “And a soft tongue breaks a bone” (Proverbs 25:15).

He saw a blind man who was straying from the road, [and] set him on his way. He saw a drunkard who was straying from the road, [and] set him on his way. He saw a wedding celebration at which they were rejoicing, [and] wept. He heard a certain man saying to a shoemaker: Make me shoes for seven years; he laughed. He saw a certain diviner divining; he laughed.

When he arrived there, they did not bring him in to Solomon for three days. On the first day he said to them: Why does the king not ask for me [to come] before him? They said to him: Drinking has overcome him. He took a brick [and] set it on top of another. They came [and] told Solomon. He said to them: This is what he was saying to you: Go back [and] give him drink.

The next day he said to them: And why does the king not ask for me [to come] before him? They said to him: Eating has overcome him. He took the brick off the other [and] set it on the ground. They came [and] told Solomon. He said to them: This is what he was saying to you: Withhold his food from him.

[At the end of] three days he went in before him. He took a reed, measured four cubits, and threw [it] down before him. He said to him: Now look, when that man dies he has nothing in this world but four cubits. Now you have conquered the whole world, and you were not satisfied until you had conquered me as well?

He said to him: I do not want anything from you. I want to build the Temple, and I need the *shamir*. He said to him: It was not entrusted to me; it was entrusted to the Prince of the Sea, and he gives it only to the wild cock, whom he trusts on its oath.

And what does it do with it? It takes it to mountains where there is no habitation and sets it on the crag of the mountain, and the mountain splits; and it gathers and brings seeds of trees and throws [them] there, and it becomes inhabited. And this is why we render [it] *naggar tura* [mountain-carpenter].

They searched out the nest of a wild cock that had young, and covered its nest with white glass. When it came, it wanted to go in and could not. It went [and] brought the *shamir* and set it on [the glass]. He shouted at it; it dropped it; he took it. It went [and] strangled itself because of its oath.

Benaiah said to him: What is the reason that, when you saw that blind man who was straying from the road, you set him on his way? He said to him: They proclaim of him in heaven that he is a completely righteous man, and whoever gives him ease merits the world to come.

And what is the reason that, when you saw that drunkard who was straying from the road, you set him on his way? He said to him: They proclaim of him in heaven that he is a completely wicked man, and I gave him ease so that he would use up [his] world.

What is the reason that, when you saw that wedding celebration, you wept? He said to him: The husband is going to die within thirty days, and she will have to wait thirteen years for a levir who is a minor.

What is the reason that, when you heard that man who said to the shoemaker, Make me shoes for seven years, you laughed? He said to him: That one has not got seven days, and he wants shoes for seven years!
What is the reason that, when you saw that diviner divining, you laughed? He said to him: Because he was sitting on a royal treasure; let him divine what is beneath him!

He kept him with him until he had built the Temple. One day he was standing alone [with him]. He said to him: It is written: “He has as it were the soaring strength of a wild ox” (Numbers 24:8), and we say: “soaring strength”: these are the ministering angels; “wild ox”: these are the *shedim*. What is your superiority over us?

He said to him: Take the chain off me and give me your ring, and I will show you my superiority. He took the chain off him and gave him his ring. He swallowed it, set one of his wings in heaven and one of his wings on earth, [and] flung him four hundred parasangs. About that hour Solomon said: “What profit has a man in all his toil that he toils under the sun?” (Ecclesiastes 1:3).

“And this was my portion from all my toil” (Ecclesiastes 2:10). What is “this”? Rav and Shmuel: one said: his staff; and one said: his cloak. He went around from door to door; wherever he came he said: “I, Kohelet, was king over Israel in Jerusalem” (Ecclesiastes 1:12). When he came to the Sanhedrin, the Rabbis said: Now, a madman does not stick to one thing. What is this?

They said to Benaiah: Does the king ask for you [to come] to him? He said to them: No. They sent to the queens: Does the king come to you? They sent [back] to them: Yes, he comes. They sent to them: Examine his feet. They sent to them: He comes in socks.

And he demands them during their menstrual impurity, and he demands also Bathsheba his mother. They brought Solomon and gave him a ring and a chain on which the Name was engraved. When he went in, he saw him [and] flew off.

And even so he was in dread of him, and this is what is written: “Behold, the bed of Solomon: sixty mighty men around it, of the mighty men of Israel, all of them gripping swords, trained in war, each man with his sword on his thigh, because of dread in the nights” (Song of Songs 3:7).
Rav and Shmuel: one said: king and commoner; and one said: king and commoner and king.
